2000-03-31: Silvio Berlusconi set sail from Genoa on a rented luxury liner, renamed Azzurra, to launch a two-week electoral comeback tour ahead of regional elections on April 16.
2000-04-17: Silvio Berlusconi's opposition bloc won landslide victories in Italy's regional elections, leading Prime Minister Massimo D'Alema to offer his resignation.
2000-04-19: Italian Prime Minister Massimo D'Alema is expected to resign to give his centre-left government a chance to rally around a new leader and avert an early general election that Silvio Berlusconi's centre-right alliance is demanding.
2000-07-04: Dino Zoff resigns as manager of Italy after Silvio Berlusconi criticised his tactics following Italy's Euro 2000 final defeat by France.
2000-09-11: Silvio Berlusconi returns to the Italian parliament as leader of the centre-right opposition, planning to topple the government and trigger a snap general election.
2000-09-25: Italian Prime Minister Giuliano Amato announced he would resign before the next general election and hand leadership of the centre-left to Francesco Rutelli, saying only the telegenic mayor could stop Silvio Berlusconi's resurgent centre-right opposition.
2001-03-13: Silvio Berlusconi, as honorary chairman of AC Milan, sacks coach Alberto Zaccheroni after the club's poor performances and Champions League exit.
2001-03-14: Silvio Berlusconi, Milan's owner, abruptly sacks coach Alberto Zaccheroni hours after the club was eliminated from the Champions League.
2001-03-28: Over 1,000 Italian intellectuals signed an appeal urging voters to oppose Silvio Berlusconi's centre-right coalition in the May 13 general election to preserve Italian democracy.
2001-04-13: Silvio Berlusconi is to send every Italian family a 128-page biography featuring 250 photographs of himself as a vote-winning ploy for the election campaign that opens today.
2001-04-30: The Madrid newspaper El Mundo claimed that Italian opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi misled a Spanish court investigating £4m tax fraud allegations at the television station Tele 5.
2001-05-13: Polling stations closed in Italy's general election, with counting underway to decide whether Silvio Berlusconi will be elected prime minister.

Silvio Berlusconi's centre-right coalition, dominated by his Forza Italia party, won enough seats in Italy's elections to secure majorities in both houses of parliament even without ally Umberto Bossi's Northern League.
Silvio Berlusconi's centre-right coalition appeared on course to win Italy's general election, according to early exit polls.
2001-05-14: Silvio Berlusconi's centre-right opposition coalition decisively wins Italy's general election, gaining majorities in both houses of parliament.
Silvio Berlusconi is set to become Italy's new prime minister after his conservative coalition appeared to win a majority in the Senate in the Italian general election.
France's foreign minister Hubert Védrine says Europe will keep a "vigilant" eye on Silvio Berlusconi's actions in office.
2001-06-07: Silvio Berlusconi threatens to launch parliamentary investigations into his left-leaning political opponents and to stage mass rallies if they try to stop him.
2001-06-25: A Milan appeal court rules that Silvio Berlusconi should not stand trial for allegedly bribing a Rome judge because the charges are covered by a statute of limitations, while in a separate case police raid the headquarters of his Mediaset broadcasting company.
2001-07-20: Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi and President Carlo Azeglio Ciampi appeared together to express sadness and plead for calm after a demonstrator was shot dead during protests at the Genoa G8 summit.
Silvio Berlusconi hosts the G8 summit in Genoa, preparing extensively for the event and aiming to improve his international image.
2001-07-27: Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi acknowledged international outrage over police brutality at the G8 summit and hinted he would purge the commanders responsible, while resisting opposition demands for a parliamentary commission of inquiry.
2001-07-28: Silvio Berlusconi faces international embarrassment over complaints about the brutality of Italian police at the Genoa summit.
2001-07-30: Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi's government signals it will accept a parliamentary inquiry into police violence at the G8 summit in Genoa, after cabinet ministers persuaded him that blocking it would be seen as a cover-up.
2001-08-03: Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi reportedly decides to move the UN Food and Agricultural Organisation's November world food summit from Rome to Africa, citing risks from anti-globalisation protests, though no formal announcement has been made.
2001-08-04: Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi reportedly decided to move the UN Food and Agricultural Organisation's November world food summit from Rome to Africa due to concerns about anti-globalisation protests, though no formal announcement was made and a spokesman declined to confirm or deny the reports.
2001-08-09: Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi visited Venice hours after a bomb blast damaged the courthouse, calling the attack a worrying escalation of violence.
2002-01-06: Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi assumes interim responsibility for foreign affairs following the resignation of Foreign Minister Renato Ruggiero.
2002-02-22: Silvio Berlusconi's government secured control of state broadcaster Rai by appointing sympathizers to its board, giving him direct and indirect control of about 90% of the Italian television market.
2002-02-24: British arts celebrities campaign against Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi to prevent the non-renewal of Mario Fortunato's contract as director of the Italian Cultural Institute in London.
2002-05-03: A Sicilian judge dismissed allegations that Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi and an associate were implicated in the 1992 murders of mafia prosecutors Giovanni Falcone and Paolo Borsellino, while asking prosecutors to reopen the investigation focusing on links between Berlusconi's Fininvest Group and Cosa Nostra.
2002-06-20: Italian magistrates stage a one-day strike against a government bill to change the judicial system, which critics say is intended to curb their independence amid Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi's corruption trial.
2002-07-12: Paolo Berlusconi, brother of Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi, was given a suspended 21-month prison sentence for bribery after plea bargaining and agreeing to pay €49m compensation to the local authority in Milan.
2002-10-06: AC Milan president Silvio Berlusconi celebrated his team's 6-0 thrashing of Torino at the San Siro.
2003-02-27: Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi faced political protest for attempting to directly nominate the heads of state television service Rai, reportedly tipping McDonald's Italy head Mario Resca to be its new president.
2003-05-23: A Milan prosecutor claimed Swiss bank account evidence proved alleged accomplices of Silvio Berlusconi bribed magistrates in the 1980s to win a corporate takeover battle.
2003-06-13: Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi is being investigated by magistrates over suspected tax fraud and false accounting related to Mediaset's acquisition of US film rights.
2003-06-14: Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi was placed under investigation for alleged tax fraud and false book-keeping related to Mediaset's alleged tax avoidance, according to Italian media reports.
2003-06-17: Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi appeared in a Milan court on bribery charges, denying the allegations, in what was expected to be his final trial appearance before parliament approves an immunity bill protecting him from prosecution.
2003-07-03: Italian Premier Silvio Berlusconi apologizes to Chancellor Gerhard Schröder for his Nazi concentration camp guard remark to a German MEP, ending the diplomatic crisis with Italy.
2003-07-08: The Italian senate began debating a controversially amended communications bill that critics say would enable Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi to extend his influence over the country's media.
2003-07-24: Two prosecutors who put Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi on trial for bribery are themselves placed under investigation for suspected abuse of office.
2003-12-16: Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi pledged to bypass an attempt to curb his media power by having his government impose an emergency decree to protect his television empire from being dismantled.
2003-12-19: Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi announces that reviewing the legislation guaranteeing parties equal access to TV air time will be a top priority in the new year, with discussion on the working agenda from January 7.
2003-12-23: The Italian cabinet passed an emergency decree to save one of Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi's private TV channels, Retequattro, overruling a court decision that it should move to satellite by year-end.
2004-01-21: Silvio Berlusconi returned to his Roman palazzo after a month-long absence from public view, during which he made only two trips to the capital to chair cabinet meetings.
2004-01-24: Silvio Berlusconi holds a rally to celebrate the 10th anniversary of his entry into politics.
2004-01-28: Silvio Berlusconi said his wife, Veronica Lario, had talked him into having cosmetic surgery during his absence.
2004-02-26: Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi comments on police raids of all 42 Serie A and Serie B clubs in a probe into financial irregularity, saying he hopes the situations that emerge will be in order.
2004-04-14: Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi's government faces criticism over its Iraq policy after the execution of Italian hostage Fabrizio Quattrocchi and threats to kill three other Italian captives.
2004-04-16: The bribery trial of Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi resumed after a 10-month adjournment, with prosecutors unsuccessfully requesting the presiding judge's removal for alleged bias.
2004-06-14: In the European elections, Lilli Gruber won twice as many votes as Silvio Berlusconi in Rome, while Berlusconi's Forza Italia party trailed the Olive Tree Alliance nationally.
2004-06-23: Opposition MPs tabled a parliamentary question claiming that work on Silvio Berlusconi's Sardinian villa began before planning permission was obtained.
2004-06-28: Silvio Berlusconi's centre-right coalition was defeated in weekend local elections, losing Milan, his home town and traditional stronghold, to the centre-left.
2004-06-30: Mediaset, the media empire of Silvio Berlusconi, acquired non-exclusive rights to broadcast home games of Juventus, Inter, and AC Milan on its digital channels for the next three seasons in a €86m deal.
2004-08-17: Italian police defused a bomb near Silvio Berlusconi's Sardinian holiday villa after a warning from a leftwing group, hours after Tony Blair's visit.
2004-11-04: The Italian government led by Silvio Berlusconi moved to strengthen the powers of the Turin Olympic Committee's supervisor, prompting committee president Valentino Castellani to announce his intention to resign.
2004-12-10: Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi was cleared of the most serious corruption charge against him when a Milan court ruled the accusation of bribing a judge was "out of time," and he was found not guilty of all other charges.
2004-12-30: Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi called for an extraordinary G8 meeting to discuss aid organization and possible debt reduction for countries affected by the Indian Ocean tsunami.
2005-02-23: David Mills, husband of UK Culture Secretary Tessa Jowell, says he has been informed that Milan magistrates are seeking to make him a defendant in the tax evasion and money laundering trial of Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi.
2005-04-09: Silvio Berlusconi committed himself to sexual abstinence until the Italian general election.
2005-04-13: Silvio Berlusconi's coalition government teeters on the brink of collapse after deep divisions emerged among his allies over Italy's economic performance and the government's vulnerability to claims of discriminating against the south.
Fininvest, the company at the apex of Silvio Berlusconi's business empire, announced it was reducing its holding in the Mediaset TV network to just over 34%.
2005-04-18: Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi agreed to resign and form a new government to strengthen his struggling conservative coalition, averting fresh elections.
2005-07-07: Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi confirmed that Italy would begin withdrawing 300 troops from Iraq in September, dependent on the security situation.
2005-07-28: Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi is suing British author David Lane and Italian publisher Editori Laterza for defamation over the book "Berlusconi's Shadow: Crime, Justice and the Pursuit of Power," seeking more than €1m in moral damages, with no court date yet set.
2005-10-24: Romano Prodi accused Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi of trying to buy election victory ahead of the next general election.
2006-02-10: Metropolitan Police officers raided the London offices of David Mills, husband of Culture Secretary Tessa Jowell, as part of an investigation into claims he was paid a bribe to lie in court for Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi.
2006-02-13: Silvio Berlusconi reportedly compared himself to Jesus Christ as a "patient victim" at a dinner with supporters, drawing criticism from leftist parliamentarians ahead of Italy's general election campaign.
2006-03-10: Italian prosecutors seek indictment of Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi and David Mills on corruption charges.
2006-04-03: Silvio Berlusconi called opponents "coglioni" during the final TV debate before Italy's general election.
2006-04-10: Italy's general election result remained too close to call, with projections showing Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi could yet retain control of both houses of parliament.
2006-04-28: It was reported that Silvio Berlusconi would resign as Italy's Prime Minister on Tuesday.
2006-05-02: Silvio Berlusconi resigned as Italian prime minister after losing the general election to a centre-left coalition.
2006-05-13: Silvio Berlusconi calls for Milan to be awarded the Serie A titles from the past two seasons amid the Juventus scandal.
2006-05-30: Anti-corruption prosecutors in Spain are considering whether to reopen a suspended investigation into alleged tax fraud involving Silvio Berlusconi's holdings in Spain's Telecinco TV channel, just two weeks after he lost immunity from prosecution.
2006-07-07: Former Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi is ordered to stand trial on charges of false accounting, embezzlement and tax fraud related to the purchase of movie and television rights at his media empire Mediaset.
2006-10-13: The Italian cabinet approves a law forcing Silvio Berlusconi's Mediaset and state broadcaster RAI to each give up one of their three terrestrial analogue channels by 2009, a decision Berlusconi calls a "political vendetta" and vows to fight in parliament.
2006-10-30: David Mills, the estranged husband of UK culture secretary Tessa Jowell, is ordered to stand trial in Italy alongside former Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi on bribery charges.
2006-11-21: Former Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi went on trial with David Mills on charges of embezzlement, tax dodging, and false accounting; the proceedings were swiftly adjourned until Monday.
2006-12-18: Silvio Berlusconi arrived in the US for scheduled medical checks, amid reports he may undergo surgery or have a pacemaker fitted.
2006-12-20: Silvio Berlusconi underwent heart surgery in Cleveland, Ohio, to correct an irregular heartbeat, which his party Forza Italia said was fully successful.
2007-08-21: Silvio Berlusconi reportedly arranged with a notary public to register the name and logos of a new "Freedom party" as he plans to found a new political movement to regain power in Italy.
2007-09-24: Lawyers for Silvio Berlusconi and David Mills prevented pivotal evidence in their Italian tax fraud trial from being heard in open court at a London mutual legal assistance hearing.
2007-11-18: Silvio Berlusconi announces he is dissolving Forza Italia to replace it with a new broader movement he intends to call the Italian People of Freedoms party.
2007-11-23: Leaked phone taps published by La Repubblica suggest Italian state television RAI and Berlusconi-owned Mediaset colluded to favor Silvio Berlusconi during his time as prime minister.
2008-01-24: Romano Prodi resigns as Italian prime minister, clearing the way for Silvio Berlusconi to bid once more to govern Italy.
2008-01-25: Silvio Berlusconi campaigns in Naples for snap April elections following Prime Minister Romano Prodi's resignation.
2008-02-05: Silvio Berlusconi was poised to launch his fifth challenge for the leadership of Italy, with opinion polls predicting a landslide victory in April's general election.
2008-04-14: Silvio Berlusconi was set to return to power as Italy's prime minister after his Freedom Folk movement won the general election, with Walter Veltroni conceding defeat.
2008-04-23: Silvio Berlusconi announces he will resign as president of Milan next month when he begins his third term as prime minister of Italy.
2008-07-07: The Bush administration apologizes to Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi after White House officials briefed the press corps with a biography describing him as a political amateur.
2009-02-20: Silvio Berlusconi's cabinet issued an emergency decree allowing mayors to enroll citizen patrols to combat crime following an outcry over rapes blamed on immigrants.
2009-04-03: Silvio Berlusconi selects former Milan and Fiorentina goalkeeper Giovanni Galli as his candidate for mayor of Florence in the June elections.
2009-05-18: Milan president Silvio Berlusconi says there are good chances Arsenal striker Emmanuel Adebayor will arrive at the club this summer.
2009-06-29: Italy's President Giorgio Napolitano urges politicians and journalists to suspend controversial discussions before the G8 summit that Silvio Berlusconi will chair, amid allegations about Berlusconi's sex life.
2009-07-07: Silvio Berlusconi dismisses a Guardian report that the US took the lead in managing the G8 summit agenda, calling it "a colossal blunder by a small newspaper."
2009-07-10: Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi hosts the G8 summit amid controversy over a Guardian report speculating Italy might be expelled from the G8.
2009-12-13: Silvio Berlusconi was injured after a man threw a model of Milan cathedral at him during a rally in Milan, and he was kept in hospital overnight.
2009-12-15: Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi remains hospitalized for another night after being struck by a model of Milan's cathedral at a political rally, suffering a broken nose and two broken teeth.
2009-12-16: Silvio Berlusconi spends a fourth night in hospital after being attacked at a political rally, as doctors again postpone a decision on his discharge.
2009-12-17: Silvio Berlusconi left hospital after spending four nights under medical supervision following an attack with a souvenir model of Milan cathedral.
2010-01-30: Silvio Berlusconi met his wife Veronica Lario in a Milan court for the first time since she announced she was leaving him, beginning divorce proceedings.
2010-02-25: Italy's highest court is expected to rule on David Mills's bribery conviction appeal, a decision that will affect Silvio Berlusconi's pending Milan corruption trial.
2010-03-15: Silvio Berlusconi was placed under investigation by Italian magistrates on suspicion of pressuring Italy's media watchdog to block a state television talk show he considered hostile.
2010-04-21: Italy's highest appeals court stated that it quashed David Mills's conviction for taking a bribe from Silvio Berlusconi due to a statute of limitations technicality, not because it believed him innocent.
2010-05-14: Leonardo leaves his post as Milan manager by mutual consent after his relationship with owner Silvio Berlusconi deteriorated following public criticism of team selection.
2010-06-29: A Sicilian appeals court ruled there was no evidence that Marcello Dell'Utri, a long-term ally of Silvio Berlusconi, had links with the Mafia after 1992, effectively clearing Berlusconi of accusations that his entry into politics was sponsored by the Mafia.
2010-11-04: Silvio Berlusconi dismissed sex and drug allegations against him as "made-up stories" and hinted the mafia may have framed him in reprisal for recent police successes.
2010-11-15: Four ministers loyal to Gianfranco Fini resigned from Silvio Berlusconi's government, bringing the administration closer to a confidence vote in parliament.
2010-11-19: Judges in Palermo ruled that Marcello Dell'Utri, who spearheaded Silvio Berlusconi's entry into politics, was also an intermediary between Berlusconi and the Sicilian mafia, and that Berlusconi paid enormous sums to Cosa Nostra for protection and to safeguard his TV network's relay stations on Sicily.
2010-12-02: Silvio Berlusconi was flying to Sochi for an unscheduled meeting with Vladimir Putin, shortly after WikiLeaks published US diplomatic cables alleging a secret business association between them.
2010-12-14: Silvio Berlusconi wins two confidence votes, avoiding resignation and blunting a rebellion by followers of former deputy Gianfranco Fini, though political uncertainty remains.
2011-01-14: Silvio Berlusconi is formally placed under investigation by Milan prosecutors on suspicion of paying for sex with a 17-year-old girl and abusing his position as prime minister to cover up the alleged relationship.
2011-01-19: A police trade union criticized the reported use of policewomen's outfits in striptease shows at Silvio Berlusconi's villa, as a parliamentary committee began considering whether to allow part of the investigation to proceed.
2011-01-21: Prosecutors investigating Silvio Berlusconi were told he would not answer their questions, as a witness, Nadia Macri, came forward with new evidence against him.
2011-02-02: Prosecutors investigating Silvio Berlusconi said they expected to recommend that the Italian prime minister be charged with abusing his position to cover up allegations that he had paid an underage prostitute.
2011-02-09: Prosecutors announce they will ask for Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi to be put on trial over his relationship with a teenager alleged to have been an underage prostitute.
2011-02-15: A Milan judge ruled that Silvio Berlusconi should stand trial on 6 April on charges of paying an underage prostitute and abusing his position as prime minister to cover it up.
2011-02-16: Silvio Berlusconi publicly stated he was not worried about standing trial on charges of paying an underage prostitute and abusing his official position.
2011-03-07: Silvio Berlusconi underwent a four-hour jaw and dental operation under general anaesthetic to repair damage from a 2009 attack, was discharged from hospital in Milan, and returned to his villa.
2011-04-02: The trial of Silvio Berlusconi on charges of paying for sex with a 17-year-old and abuse of office is set to begin in Italy.
2011-04-05: Italian MPs vote to challenge the legitimacy of Silvio Berlusconi's underage prostitution trial, setting up a constitutional face-off that could derail the case.
2011-04-06: Silvio Berlusconi's trial on charges of paying an underage prostitute and abusing his office formally opened in Milan, with the alleged escort declining to attach herself to the case.
2011-04-11: Silvio Berlusconi denied accusations that he paid a teenage runaway for sex, saying he gave €45,000 to Karima el Mahroug to help her launch a beauty business.
2011-04-18: Three associates under investigation in a related prostitution case against Silvio Berlusconi fell out, with Nicole Minetti's defense document reportedly blaming Emilio Fede and Lele Mora for introducing the prime minister to Karima El Mahroug, while Fede denied the memorandum and accused Mora.
2011-05-06: Milan prosecutors ask for an Anglo-Italian former showgirl and two others to be put on trial for allegedly procuring 33 young women for so-called bunga bunga sex sessions at Silvio Berlusconi's home.
2011-05-29: Voters in Milan go to the polls in a mayoral runoff widely seen as a crucial test of Silvio Berlusconi's diminished political standing, after a minister resigned over his remarks about Italy's judges.
2011-05-30: Silvio Berlusconi suffered a humiliating political defeat in his home city of Milan when his party's candidate for mayor, Letizia Moratti, was ousted in a runoff by leftwing lawyer Giuliano Pisapia.
2011-07-09: A Milan appeals court ordered Silvio Berlusconi's company Fininvest to pay over €560m in compensation to rival Carlo De Benedetti for bribery of a judge in the battle for control of publisher Mondadori, with the judges stating Berlusconi was "jointly responsible" for the corruption.
2011-09-01: Two people alleged to have blackmailed Silvio Berlusconi were arrested in Rome.
2011-10-26: Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi's government released a letter to European Union authorities outlining reforms, including public asset sales and employment law changes, to address Italy's debt crisis.

Silvio Berlusconi's coalition government edged closer to breaking up as he struggled to draw up economic reforms to satisfy EU leaders, with Northern League leader Umberto Bossi expressing pessimism about the government's survival.
2011-11-03: Silvio Berlusconi's resignation became a question of when, not if, as his majority in parliament was thrown into doubt by deserting MPs.
2011-11-08: Silvio Berlusconi informs Italy's president that he will resign as prime minister after passing EU-demanded economic reforms, though he says it will be sometime in November.
2011-11-12: Silvio Berlusconi resigns as Italian prime minister.
2011-11-25: Silvio Berlusconi fails in a legal bid to stop David Mills from giving evidence in his corruption trial.
2011-11-28: Testimony of David Mills in Silvio Berlusconi's bribery trial was delayed as lawyers and judges debated how he should give evidence via video link to the Milan court.
2012-02-25: A bribery trial against former Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi over payments to British lawyer David Mills failed to reach a verdict after judges ruled the statute of limitations had expired.
2012-07-14: Silvio Berlusconi gave the clearest indication yet that he will seek re-election as Italian prime minister in 2013.
2012-10-19: George Clooney is called as a witness in Silvio Berlusconi's trial in Milan, where Berlusconi is accused of paying an underage prostitute for sex.
2012-10-26: Milan owner Silvio Berlusconi was found guilty of tax fraud and sentenced to four years in prison, with a three-year ban from public office, in a case involving Mediaset film and television rights; he denied wrongdoing and is expected to appeal.
2012-10-27: Silvio Berlusconi says a tax fraud verdict against him is politically motivated.
2012-12-08: Silvio Berlusconi confirms he will run again for prime minister of Italy.
2012-12-10: Judges in Milan ordered a nationwide hunt for Karima el-Mahroug after she failed to appear in court to testify in Silvio Berlusconi's trial on charges of paying for underage sex.
2012-12-12: Berlusconi said he would withdraw from the election race if Mario Monti agreed to stand for office at the head of a coalition that included his Freedom People party.
2013-01-09: Senior judges in Milan rebuke Silvio Berlusconi after he blamed his large alimony payments on "feminist, communist" magistrates.
2013-01-14: A Milan court rejected Silvio Berlusconi's request to suspend his trial over charges of paying for sex with an underage prostitute and abuse of office, ordering proceedings to continue despite his election campaign.
2013-01-15: Milan owner Silvio Berlusconi apologizes for calling Mario Balotelli "a rotten apple" but claims neither he nor vice-president Adriano Galliani have discussed buying the Manchester City striker.
2013-01-29: AC Milan, owned by Silvio Berlusconi, agreed a deal for Mario Balotelli to leave Manchester City, with the timing during the January transfer window prompting political rivals to question whether it was intended to win votes ahead of parliamentary elections.
2013-02-03: Paolo Berlusconi, brother of former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi, used a racial slur to describe Mario Balotelli before the footballer's first match for AC Milan.
2013-04-04: Karima "Ruby" el-Mahroug, the woman at the center of Silvio Berlusconi's sex trial, accused prosecutors of psychological warfare and denied having sex with Berlusconi, while admitting she had lied about her origins.
2013-05-13: Prosecutors in the Rubygate trial demand that Silvio Berlusconi serve six years in prison and be banned from public office for life for allegedly paying for sex with an underage prostitute and abusing his office to cover it up.
2013-06-24: A verdict is expected in Silvio Berlusconi's trial in Milan on charges of paying for sex with an underage girl and abusing his office to cover it up.
2013-07-10: Italy's parliament was suspended after the Democratic Party joined Silvio Berlusconi's followers in voting for a stoppage in protest at a supreme court decision to fast-track his final appeal against a tax fraud conviction.
2013-07-30: Italy's supreme court is due to decide on Silvio Berlusconi's final appeal against a tax fraud conviction, which if upheld could bar him from public office for five years.
2013-08-01: Italy's supreme court upheld Silvio Berlusconi's fraud conviction, his first definitive conviction, triggering a political crisis over whether the senate will expel him.
2013-08-13: Italian President Giorgio Napolitano says Silvio Berlusconi's definitive tax fraud conviction must be respected and warns that a government crisis over the issue would be fatal.
2013-09-29: Silvio Berlusconi called for fresh Italian elections as soon as possible after pulling his ministers out of Enrico Letta's grand coalition government.
2013-10-03: Silvio Berlusconi announced he would instruct his party to vote against a motion of no confidence in Enrico Letta's coalition government, a tacit admission that he had lost the backing of a sizable number of his own politicians and no longer had power of veto over government policy.
2013-10-06: Silvio Berlusconi's lawyer says he intends to request that Berlusconi serve his one-year tax fraud sentence through a community service placement.
2013-11-27: Italy's upper house of parliament voted to oust Silvio Berlusconi following his conviction for tax fraud.
2014-01-21: Pier Silvio Berlusconi reportedly threatened to close two Mediaset programmes, including Domenica Live, unless they cut or toned down sexual content, following an internal investigation and a parents' movement complaint.
2014-04-11: Marcello Dell'Utri, a close ally of former Italian Premier Silvio Berlusconi, was apprehended in Beirut after fleeing Italy as a fugitive.
2014-04-15: A Milan court rules that former Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi will serve his year-long tax fraud sentence through part-time community service at a home for the elderly.
2014-06-06: Milan president Silvio Berlusconi said the club would decide on a solution for coach Clarence Seedorf at the next board meeting, describing him as part of the club's past.
2014-07-18: A Milan appeals court acquitted former Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi of charges of paying for sex with an underage prostitute and abusing his office to cover it up, overturning a prior conviction.
2015-01-29: Italy begins the process of electing a new president, a vote expected to measure the political relevance of Silvio Berlusconi, who remains at the helm of the centre-right opposition party Forza Italia.
2015-05-29: Silvio Berlusconi mistakenly arrived at a leftist party rally in Segrate, Italy, instead of his own Forza Italia event.
2016-04-12: AC Milan president Silvio Berlusconi met with youth coach Cristian Brocchi over a three-hour dinner before deciding to sack Sinisa Mihajlovic and appoint Brocchi as first-team coach until the end of the season.
2016-06-14: Silvio Berlusconi underwent heart surgery to replace a faulty aortic valve and was placed in intensive care.
